correctness.rationale: For all integers \(v\ge2\), \(1\le k<v\), all finite widths, and complex coefficients \(a,b\), center each binary column and the coordinate rows. The common squared lengths \((v-1)/v\) and \(k(v-k)/v\) give the upper norm bound \(\left|a+bk/v\right|+|b|\sqrt{k(v-k)(v-1)}/v\) via a one-parameter Schur factorization and exact minimization. The complete \(k\)-subset incidence matrix has \(NN^*=(r-\lambda)I+\lambda J\) with \(r-\lambda=nk(v-k)/[v(v-1)]\), yielding a constant singular value \(\sqrt{vn}|a+bk/v|\) and \(v-1\) further singular values \(|b|\sqrt{r-\lambda}\). The rectangular polar witness yields a universal nuclear-trace lower bound \(\|M\|_*/\sqrt{vn}\) that exactly matches the upper bound. The proof explicitly covers \(a+bk/v=0\), \(b=0\), and \(k=1\). Real coefficients have real bounds and witnesses. The balanced-column width minimum follows from the Frobenius norm and a normalized Hadamard example. Actual standalone code checked 180 complete incidence and 1155 random support instances; these finite computations are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Sparse operator masks with a prescribed number \(k\) of incidences per column are natural in rectangular Schur multiplication. The result gives one sharp finite-\(v,k\) functional-analytic constant for every two-level complex symbol and every finite width, not merely a table or a single example. Complete hypergraph incidences establish equality without requiring symmetry of an arbitrary input. The zero-one and signed cases, the sharp balanced-\(k=v/2\) deficit \(\sqrt{v-1}\) with Hadamard minimal widths, and the sparse-negative limit \(1+2\sqrt{k}\) are meaningful structural boundaries. This is a natural complete extremal classification with a self-contained derivation, independent of a downstream theorem.
